title: THE CENSORSHIP STORM
about: Three travelers cross a desert where censor bars fall like hail: the Regent's rules, the Podcaster's pinned slogan, the plan to talk only in forms, and the basement where the Shepherd's questions make the storm hesitate.

beats.text: The desert of Texas, late afternoon. Two travelers on foot. The wind rises carrying paperwork, and then black bars fall from the sky. Whatever a bar lands on is erased.
That’s… that’s new.
What is a storm but a law with weather?
Then, with no footsteps at all, a third man is simply there. The Regent, an official in a dark suit, carrying scissors that are also a pen.
see: a man in a dark suit standing in the desert
a pair of scissors cutting paper

beats.text: You have exceeded your daily allotment of meaning.
Is meaning private property?
Meaning is communal. And therefore regulated. Even I hate this.

beats.ask: you can't say anything anymore these days

beats.text: Say something true. Say something punishable.
Okay. Watch this. I am pro—
A bar slams across his chest and pins him flat to the sand.
see: a man lying face down in the sand

beats.text: —monetization! I was gonna say pro-monetization!
Is profit a form of prayer?
With one snip of his pen, the Regent edits him free.
see: a man helping another man up from the ground

beats.text: Thanks. I hate you.
You’re welcome. It’s required.
Do we escape by silence?
The storm isn’t hunting you. It’s hunting assertions.
So… no opinions.
No advocacy. No slogans. No “should.” Only questions, definitions, and administrative language.

beats.ask: keep your head down and fill in the forms

beats.text: If you carry a form, the storm assumes you belong to it.
Finally. A religion I understand.
Carrying their forms, they walk the desert road to shelter: a diner half-buried in sand. In its basement, a projector plays an old oil commercial on a loop.
see: a film projector in a dark room

beats.text: Are we watching truth, or watching ourselves watching truth?
Don’t get poetic. Poetry triggers the storm.
A bar crashes through the ceiling and lands upright, like a tombstone. On it, in white letters: metaphor detected.
So it does understand art.
It doesn’t understand art. It understands risk.
Is censorship a storm… or is it an alibi?

beats.ask: it's just an excuse, that's all it is

beats.text: The bar trembles and falls apart into Greek letters on the floor. Overhead, for the first time, the storm hesitates between blows.
see: old printing type scattered on a floor

beats.text: Stop. Stop doing philosophy.
So… we just keep asking questions until the storm gets tired?
Is that not how every state ends?
